It is a resplendent plane of majestic marble halls, gleaming palaces, and heavenly radiance. ==Inhabitants== The enormous central mountain, [[Celestia]], is the home of the [[celestial archon|archon]]s, ruled by [[Zaphkiel]], and is something of a divine realm itself, though no deity lives there. Many of them live on the other surrounding mountains, serving [[Helm]], [[Ilmater]], [[Torm]], or [[Tyr]]. [[Angel]]s serve the [[Triad]] as well, and take on the bulk of the missions to other planes. Also, [[formian]]s live here and serve both Helm and Siamorphe on occasion, but generally they live ordered lives without interruption from the divine. ==Petitioners== Most of the petitioners here are [[lantern archon]]s, who have no planar commitment and can leave the House at will. Those who follow Helm or Siamorphe, or otherwise lean more toward neutrality than good, keep the forms they wore in life. They gain the benefits of immunity to electrical attacks, cannot be petrified, and are able to withstand phyical attacks better than they did in life. ==Deities== * '''[[Helm]]''' - The Vigilant One, resides on [[Everwatch]], which is a floating watchtower of the plane. Whenever a visitor comes to this plane, Everwatch is there with its guardian. The guardian, covered in a suit of ''mithral'' full plate, detects the alignment and purposes of visitors and can call heavenly defenders in the case of invasion. * '''[[Ilmater]]''' - The Crying god, rules on the mountain known as [[Martyrdom]], and has a great open-air temple where the souls of the petitioners are rewarded for their endurance and perseverance in life. No one can feel pain or fatigue here. Ilmater's realm is known as a place of comfort and rest. * '''[[Torm]]''' - The True Deity's realm is the mountain called [[Trueheart]]. Torm's palace is in the heart of the realm and resembles a huge military fortress, with walls of [[mithral]], battlements of [[diamond]], and gates of [[adamantine]]. It is guarded by legions of [[angel]]s and [[Celestial archon|archons]] serving the cause of good and law. * '''[[Tyr]]''' - The Just god rules the third mountain which is crowned with [[The Court]]. This is where the Triad frequently consult. Whenever there is need for a trial amongst the gods, Tyr serves as judge. No one can lie or bluff here. * '''[[Siamorphe]]''' - Between the Court and Celestia lies a beautiful valley. This is the realms of Siamorphe, who lives in an Alabaster Palace, surrounded by perfect gardens and fountains. * '''[[Bahamut]]''' - Co-ruled Mercuria, the second heaven of Celestia, during his time as a [[celestial paragon]]. He returned to Celestia after it had had been cast off onto the [[Astral Sea]] when he replaced Tyr as god of justice. ==Access to the House of the Triad== There are no known ''portals'' to or from the House of the Triad, however, it is connected to other [[celestial plane]]s through branches of the [[World Tree]]. ==Appendix== ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Sources=== * {{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|159-160}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:World Tree planes]] [[Category:Celestial planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Articles lacking in-text citations]] [[Category:Locations on the World Tree]]

The '''Incanterium''' are a [[faction]], turned [[sect]], turned faction once again. They believe that wizardly magic is the secret to the multiverse.
== History ==
The Incanterium collected every magical item and scrap of magical lore in the Tower Sorcerous, which loomed over the Clerk's Ward. Factions would trade magic for help or knowledge. There came a time when the factions gradually came to be dancing on the Magicians' leash.
Then the Tower Sorcerous vanished. Rumors flew that the [[Lady of Pain]] sent the whole structure to the [[Maze]]s. Centuries passed, and the Incanterium were forgotten.
But some were still left over, wandering the planes, calling themselves '''incantifiers''', pursuing their goal of learning all the magic in the multiverse.
... and then, one day, the Tower Sorcerous reappeared.
== Philosophy ==
Incantifiers believed magic was the ultimate power of the planes: archmages would redefine the laws of their worlds, even gods feared it. You could control the entire multiverse, if only you learned enough magic. It has, after all, been done before.

The '''Industrial Stitches''' are an ore preparation facility and trolley-track switchyard running between the [[Great Foundry]] and the [[Ditch]]. Workers import ore from the cargo brought in from the Ditch, and sort them via various trolley carts intended for various Foundry destinations.
The various criss-crossing tracks resemble a series of catgut-stitched wounds when viewed [[Directions in Sigil|chordwise]], from Sigil's opposite side, giving the location its name.
Given all the filth and industrial waste surrounding the area (and transported through it), the Industrial Stitches are a major contributor to the pollution levels of the Ditch. The practice of dumping waste has brought the ire of the [[Beautification League]], whose protests have required the [[Believers of the Source]] and [[Harmonium]] to post guards along the fences.
The League has sent petitions to the [[Hall of Records]] and filed charges at the [[City Court]], but most simply dismiss them as a lunatic fringe.

The network was used by deities to traverse from the Realms to their home planes. The root or base of the Infinite Staircase was located in [[Selûne]]'s palace of [[Argentil]] in the [[Gates of the Moon]]. It only appeared if the moon was full and when the fog from the waters surrounding the palace filled the hall.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|154-155}} Multiple roughly carved landings of the stairway were also found on each of the three layers of [[Ysgard]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|91}} ===Known Entrances=== Some of the known entrances to the Celestial Stairway could be found: * Near the ruins of [[Castle Kilgrave]] in [[Cormyr]] * Near the Temple of [[Lathander]] in [[Shadowdale]]{{Cite book/Shadowdale/MMP (1989)|234}} * Near a griffon eyrie on [[Mount Waterdeep]].{{Cite book/Waterdeep|328}} ==Description== {{fq | text = Oh, the [[River Styx]] is a putrid stream,
[[Oceanus]] is too good for me.
[[Mount Olympus|Olympus]] takes too long to climb,
[[Yggdrasil]] is just a tree.
But the Infinite Staircase takes you there.
The Grand Old Stair goes ev'rywhere.
A few short steps will bring us home…
  and fulfill our ev'ry dream.
| source = Unknown planar poet{{Template:Cite book/For Duty & Deity|15}} | float = | width = 385px }} The individual stairways, invisible to ordinary people, could only be seen properly by gods or by very powerful mortals potent in [[magic]].{{Cite book/Waterdeep|326}} When made visible to others, they appeared to constantly change shape, such as a long wooden spiral staircase, a marble ladder, a pathway of [[amber]] and [[pearl]], or stranger forms. The goddess Selûne showed it to her friends as a glowing silver ribbon rising into the sky. ==History== During the [[Time of Troubles]] of the [[1358 DR|Year of Shadows, 1358 DR]], the god [[Helm]] guarded the Stairway and prevented [[Waukeen]] and [[Lliira]] from using it to return to the [[Outlands]] from Shadowdale. Helm, obviously, was not tempted by Waukeen's bribes.{{Cite book/For Duty & Deity|3}} Later that year, the Celestial Stairway appeared on Mount Waterdeep, seemingly in readiness for someone to pass between the planes and the realms, or because someone already had. [[Luna]], [[avatar]] of the goddess Selûne, was shocked to see the Stairway and made it visible to her friends [[Vajra Valmeyjar]], [[Kyriani Agrivar]], [[Onyx the Invincible]], and [[Timoth Eyesbright]]. Luna thought it signified Lord [[Ao]] was planning something. ==Rumors & Legends== The connection between the Infinite Staircase and the Gates of the Moon was suspected to be a consequence of the presence of [[Shaundakul]] in the plane. ==Notable Locations== [[File:Nowhere_inn-2e.jpg|thumb|300px|''The Nowhere Inn was a popular waypoint for travelers along the Infinite Staircase.'']] * The [[Nowhere Inn]], a community of tents and other structures located on one of the stair's wider landings.{{Cite book/For Duty & Deity|20-22}} ==Inhabitants== [[Lillend]]i lived on and guarded the Celestial Stairway. ==Appendix== {{Incomplete}} ===Appearances=== :;Adventures ::''[[Tales from the Infinite Staircase]]'' • ''[[For Duty & Deity]]'' :;Novels ::[[Shadowdale (novel)|''Shadowdale'']] • [[Waterdeep (novel)|''Waterdeep'']] :;Comics ::''[[Total Eclipse]]'' ===Further Reading=== * {{Cite book/Tales from the Infinite Staircase}} ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Magical locations]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Planar pathways]] [[Category:Locations in the Gates of the Moon]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Locations in the World Tree planes]] [[Category:Locations in Argentil]]

'''Io's Blood Isles''' are an archipelago inhabited primarily by dragons on an unknown world in the [[Prime Material plane]].
== Portals ==
The following portals are known to link to Io's Blood Isles:
* A window in [[Harbinger House]] looks out over the Isles.<ref name="hh52">{{b|Planescape|Harbinger House (book)|alt=Harbinger House|pdf=17277|page=52}}</ref> * The [[Seafarer's Arch]] in the [[Ditch]] links to Io's Blood Isles<ref name="poly137-15">{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 137|page=15}}</ref>
== Gods ==
* [[Io]], the dragon god
== Background Information ==
* '''Io's Blood Isles''' is the primary setting for the ''Council of Wyrms'' campaign setting. The name of the world is not known, just the dragons' archipelago. * The name is not "the Blood Isles belonging to Io" but "the isles made of Io's Blood." According to local myth, the dragon god Io, in seeing the strife between different species of dragon, said "if blood is to be spilled, let it be mine." He slashed his belly, and the blood fell to earth, forming the island chain.

{{Deity|name=Isis|primordial=|title=Lady of Knowledge|symbol=Eye and teardrop|power=Intermediate Power|pantheon=[[Pharaonic pantheon]]|serves=[[Ra]]|gender=Feminine|realm=[[Gizekhtet]], [[Heliopolis]]; [[Quietude]]|cleric alignments=Good|alignment=Lawful Good|portfolio=Marriage, magic, motherhood}} '''Isis''' was an Intermediate Power of the [[Pharaonic pantheon]], the child of [[Geb]] and [[Nut]] and a member of [[Ra]]'s Ennead family.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|84}}</ref> She was said to have knowledge of everything between heaven and earth, including Ra's true name and the mysteries of creation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|88}}</ref>
Isis had a keen interest in mortals, and granted many gifts to her worshippers including magic and marriage. She ruled the Second Realm of [[Heliopolis]], Gizekhtet, as well as her own private realm [[Quietude]] in [[Elysium]]. Although Heliopolis was home to her husband and many of her faithful, she preferred Quietude for its peaceful community and research opportunities.<ref name=":0" />

In the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] it was the [[divine realm]] only of the gods of the [[Frost giant|frost]] and [[fire giant]]s, [[Thrym]] and [[Surtr]], respectively. It was located on [[Ysgard]]'s [[Ysgard (layer)|first layer]].<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" />
==Description== ===Cosmography=== Usually, Jotunheim bordered the realms of [[Asgard]] and [[Vanaheim]].<ref name="MotP1e-pp94-96">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|95-96}}</ref> The Iving River, the largest river in all of Asgard, served as the border between it and Jotunheim.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p112">{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|112}}</ref><ref name="MotP1e-pp94-96" /> The realm of [[Muspelheim]] was situated behind a barrier of continually active volcanoes.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" />
===Geography=== This plane consisted of a glaciers, snow-capped mountains, volcanoes, and desolate plains.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /> Much of the landscape was dotted with [[menhir]]s and forests of towering [[pine]] and [[oak]] trees.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" /> Some described the vegetation on this plain as sickly, such as yellowing [[mistletoe]] and scraggly weeds.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" />
==Notable Locations== * [[Gudheim|'''Gudheim''']]''',''' the crystal palace of [[Annam All-Father]] before he departed to the [[Hidden Realm]] in the [[Outlands]] in his exile.<ref name="GC2e-p44">{{Cite book/Giantcraft|44}}</ref> * '''Fimbulwinter''', sometimes known as Jotunheim, was the domain of the giant god [[Thrym]] in the World Tree cosmology. Some claimed he maintained no permanent palace in the realm,<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" /> while others believed he had a massive palace of ice.<ref name="FB-p56">{{Cite book/Frostburn|56}}</ref> * '''Florallium''', the domain of the giant goddess [[Iallanis]]. It was large, peaceful palace full of gardens and crystal springs. It was an unspoken rule that the domain was a neutral territory for Jotunheim's deities and [[petitioners]], a place where peaces could be negotiated.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /> * [[Meerrauk|'''Meerrauk''']], an enormous underground city. In the Great Wheel cosmology, Surtur was said to reside within it.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /> * '''Okalnir ''' a beer-hall ran by a frost giant named [[Brimir]]. It was typically very active in the summer time, but quite deserted during winter.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /> * '''River Iving''', a river that connected the planes of Jotunheim with Asgard. A clan of [[mountain giant]]s ran a ferry that transported travelers along it.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /> * '''[[Shatterstone]]''', the domain of the [[ogre]] god [[Vaprak]]. It was a pitiful cave at the base of a great cliff.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" /> * '''The [[Steading]]''', the domain of the giant god [[Grolantor]]. A large wooden house that stood on the foothills of one of Jotunheim's many mountains.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" /> * '''Stormhold''', the domain of the giant god [[Stronmaus]]. A massive white cloud, atop which stood a palace made of various precious metals and gems, that roamed across Jotunheim bringing rain and light storms.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" /> * '''[[Thraotor]]''', the domain of the giant god [[Memnor]]. A massive thunderhead cloud, atop which stood a palace of [[adamantine]], that roamed across Jotunheim spreading violent storms in its wake.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161">{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|160-161}}</ref> * '''Utgard''', a major city and fortress that was guarded by various illusions and camouflage. It was ruled by a giant king named [[Utgard-Loki]].<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /> * [[Well of Mimir]], a legendary magical well that was situated close to one of [[Yggdrasil]]'s roots.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" /><ref name="MotP1e-pp94-96" /> * '''Woodhaven''', the domain of the giant goddess [[Hiatea]]. It was a large collection of great longhouses within the heart of a massive oak forest.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" />
==Inhabitants== The giants who inhabited Jotunheim were noted as being somewhat smarter than their relatives on the [[Material Plane]] and they were said to possess giant-sized [[Magical item|magical items]] with the power to affect a [[deity]].<ref name="MotP1e-pp94-96" /> Some considered them to be a low form of [[quasi-deity]].<ref name="DaD-p200">{{Cite book/Deities and Demigods|200}}</ref>
One could also find [[fensir]],<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" /> [[Ysgardian dwarves]], and [[gnomes]] within this realm. Though the latter two were detested by the resident giants. The dwarves often brought wares from their home layer of [[Nidavellir]] and charged double what they normally would.<ref name="Poc-BoC2e-p115-116" />
Notable animals within this realm included [[roc]]s and [[winter wolves]] that were the size of [[elephant]]s.<ref name="PGtF-p160-161" />

The '''Knife in the River''' is an ancient pockmarked triangle of metal plunged tip-first into the waters of the [[Ditch]]. The top edge is sheared and twisted. Like a knife, one edge remains sharp, despite the rust.
== History ==
The first vessel to enter [[Sigil]] via the [[Seafarer's Arch]] was a resplendent ship, its aristocratic crew of [[arcane]] under the command of an imposing [[giff]] admiral. Unfortunately the ship was wider than the Ditch, and so it ran aground.
Mere moments later, the [[Lady of Pain]] appeared, and advanced on the ship.
The arcane crew, the giff admiral, and the [[Spellweaver]] mage let loose enough destructive force to topple Sigil from the Spire. The barrage let loose from the ship's bombard is said to have been heard all the way out to the [[gate-town]]s. The blast did what no one thought possible: it wounded the Lady, shearing one of the blades off the halo of knives around her face.
Before her blade had met the water of the Ditch, her shadow sliced the ship into pieces to clear the waterway. Even today, people call an anonymous shriek in the night "the Lady's satisfaction."
The rubble, now called the [[Arcane Remains]], poke out of the water like broken ribs, with most Cagers too fearful of whatever may have earned the Lady's wrath to search the rubble. And not far from the Remains lies what's left of the Lady's lost blade, buried point-first in the Ditch: the Knife in the River.
== Background Information == * The Knife, in reference, seems to be far larger than would be assumes if it were "just" a knife from the Lady's head. The Ditch is deep enough to allow ships to travel through it, so the Knife is at least long enough to be plunged into the Ditch's bottom, and still have a substantial part of it sticking out of the water. * The "Knife in the River" is a play on the common phrase "a fork in the road."

Her Serenity, the '''Lady of Pain''', is an enigmatic figure who rules over [[Sigil]]. She largely doesn't care for the day-to-day operation of the city, happy to leave that to groups like the [[Fraternity of Order]], [[Harmonium]], and [[Mercykillers]]. What rules she has are few:
[[File:LadyofPainLineart.png|thumb|right|The Lady of Pain's stamp, used on official documents]]
# Keep the peace. ## Don't threaten the safety of the city or its portals ## Don't question the Lady's power # Don't worship her. # No gods within the city.<ref name="pscssab6365">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=63-65, Sigil and Beyond}}</ref>
Additionally, she seems to have a distaste for the [[mercane]], who feel distinctly uncomfortable within Sigil, although they are not barred to entry<ref name="psmca10">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Monstrous Compendium Appendix|page=10}}</ref>. This distaste came to most peoples' awareness during the events surrounding the creation of the [[Arcane Remains]] in the [[Ditch]].<ref name="poly137">{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 137|page=14-17}}</ref>
She is always silent; whenever she makes a pronouncement to the public, she does so via her [[dabus]] attendants, who are as inextricably part of the city as she is.
The Lady appears as a tall woman with a bladed headdress surrounding her face, although the blades are actually a part of her face.<ref name="dvd130">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=130}}</ref> Her body form cannot be determined as she wears long robes, but is presumed to be humanoid. She at least seems to have arms, although they remain tucked into the sleeves of her robe. She never walks, but floats above the city street. The [[Lady's Ward]] (never the "Lady's Ward" always "The Lady's Ward") is named after her, simply because most of her appearances seemed to be in this Ward.<ref name="pscssab79">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=79, Sigil and Beyond}}</ref>
== History == As far as anyone knows, the Lady has always been part of Sigil. The Guvners and Signers suggest she created the city.
A long time ago, no one is sure when, the Lady was on her rounds, floating through the streets. A little girl ran up to her, big smile on her face, and said something to the Lady. Either the Lady was very moved, or did not notice the young girl at all, but she escaped the encounter unscathed. The event is celebrated annually as the Day of [[Grace]], the Sigilian celebration of the New Year.<ref name="poly127-23">{{b|Polygon|Polygon Magazine 127|page=23, The Day of Grace: Sigil's New Year Holiday}}</ref>
At some point in prehistory, the powerful wizard [[Gifad]] attempted a vast spell, woven into the streets of the [[Ward of Masks]], which would grant him control over the city. At the climax of the spell, the Lady appeared, trapping him in a [[Labyrinth Stone]], and telepathically telling him, ''None but you may unlock this jewel, and then only from without. Thus you are snared, till eons hence.'' The gem is then cast into the Lower Planes.<ref name="fw112113">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=112-113}}</ref>
* Approx [[prehistory|10,000 BFHR]]: The wizard [[Shekelor]] retrieved the Labyrinth Stone and attempted to repeat Gifad's spell, but failed. For his efforts, he was burned from within in front of the [[City Courts]].<ref name="itc73">{{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|page=73}}</ref><ref name="uncaged63">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|page=63}}</ref><ref name="fw34">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=34}}</ref>
* [[Prehistory|3373 BFHR]]: Worship of [[Aoskar]], the God of Portals, rises to a degree that people begin to question the Lady's power. She destroys [[Aoskar]], his body left to float lifeless in the [[Astral Plane]]. His [[Shattered Temple|temple]] is shattered, his worship is forbidden, his image eradicated.<ref name="dttu28">{{b|Planescape|Doors to the Unknown|pdf=17290|page=28}}</ref>
* [[874 BFHR]]: The [[Expansionist]] factol [[Vartus Timlin]] is [[Maze]]d while taking a break from a meeting where he was planning a takeover of Sigil.<ref name="itc73">{{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|page=73}}</ref><ref name="uncaged42">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|page=42}}</ref><ref name="uncaged89">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|page=89}}</ref>
* [[503 BFHR]]: The [[Great Upheaval]]: After the city's 50 [[faction]]s devolved to fighting in the streets, the Lady makes one of her rare pronouncements, delivered via dabus: ''By order of the Lady of Pain, there will be but 15 factions in Sigil. Organize thy colors by a fortnight hence — or die.''
* [[117 YFHR]]: The [[First Eschaton]]: A year of bad omens. People have bad dreams and uneasy visions, the [[Lady of Pain]] make an inauspicious 13 appearances in the short timeframe of 23 days, and [[Mercykiller]] [[Factol]] [[Votohm]] dies under mysterious circumstances.<ref name="fw64">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=64}}</ref>
* [[121 YFHR]]: The bard [[Trolan]] of [[Ecstasy]] arrives in [[Sigil]] and finds a tavern to perform in. He performs a song of love to the [[Lady of Pain]]. The crowd flees and he's kicked out, with the expectation that the Lady would quickly arrive to dispatch him, but she never does. He's quickly branded Trolan the Mad. The [[Mercykillers]] were ready to deal with him when the [[dabus]] showed up to take him to [[Harbinger House]].<ref name="hh11">{{b|Planescape|Harbinger House (book)|alt=Harbinger House|pdf=17277|page=11}}</ref>
* [[127 YFHR]]: [[Trolan]] is let out of Harbinger House and is convinced that the Lady loves him back; he starts a cult of worshippers called [[Those Who Love the Lady]]. A gathering of cultists is flayed alive in [[Bloodgem Park]].<ref name="hh31">{{b|Planescape|Harbinger House (book)|alt=Harbinger House|pdf=17277|page=31}}</ref>
* [[130 YFHR]]: The [[Faction War]]. In an attempt to forestall simmering tensions, the Lady of Pain sends all the factols and other faction leaders to the [[Maze]]s over the course of two weeks, ending with the Mazing of Duke [[Rowan Darkwood]], just as he is about to release the force of the [[Labyrinth Stone]]. It doesn't work; having their leaders vanish only escalates conflict. After a month, she shuts down all the city's portals.<ref name="fw130-131">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=130-131}}</ref> After the conflict seems to end, portals are reopened, but the Lady makes a new pronouncement: ''This city tolerates your faction no longer. Abandon it or die.'' Unsure if by "it" she means "your faction" or "the city," various factions either splinter, merge, or leave Sigil entirely.<ref name="fw114">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=114}}</ref>
* [[132 YFHR]]: The Lady is caught between a rock and a hard place as the lich-lord [[Vecna]] exploits a loophole to twist his way into Sigil on his path to godhood. She can do little about his presence directly, but opening the gates to allow other gods entry will upset the balance of the city and perhaps the multiverse. Eventually she puts her faith in a group of mortal adventurers.<ref name="dvd129130">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=129130}}</ref>
== Origins ==
No one knows. Hypotheses remain rampant: * A greater [[power]]<ref name="pscssab62">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=62, Sigil and Beyond}}</ref> * A reformed [[tanar'ri]] lord<ref name="pscssab62">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=62, Sigil and Beyond}}</ref><ref name="ohg52">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|page=52}}</ref> * Hatched from a [[dabus]] egg<ref name="itc22">{{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|page=22}}</ref> * A powerful human mage, the first to control [[Sigil]]<ref name="ohg52">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|page=52}}</ref> * A hatchling from a draconic deity<ref name="ohg52">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|page=52}}</ref> * One of the [[Ancient Brethren]]<ref name="dvd129">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=129}}</ref>
== Abilities ==
Those who violate her commandments are typically subject to one of two punishments:
* '''Control of all portals''': Every portal in or out of the city exists at the Lady's whim, which explains why fiends haven't overrun the place. She's known to have shut down every portal simultaneously only once, during the [[Faction War]]. * '''They're sent to the [[Maze]]s''': if the target is walking through the city alone, that portion of the city will be taken, multiply in size and warp back in on itself to form a maze, and then cast into the [[Ethereal plane]] as a [[demiplane]]. * '''Flaying flesh''': The Lady makes a physical appearance. Either her gaze or the edges of her passing shadow will flay the flesh of the target. * '''Time manipulation''', possibly
Those who worship her tend to get flayed, while other infractions typically result in getting Mazed. It's arguable whether flaying is better or worse than centuries of being trapped in a Maze alone.
Her ability to flay with her presence may be beyond her control; the streets certainly empty out quickly when she passes, just in case.
Curiously, about [[prehistory|10,000]] years ago when the wizard [[Shekelor]] attempted his takeover of Sigil, his journey ended with him burning from within in front of the [[City Courts]], so it's possible the Lady wasn't always able to create Mazes.
The Lady seems to have some awareness of and ability to manipulate time, although this ability was ultimately only witnessed by Duke [[Rowan Darkwood]] and the wizard [[Gifad]].
== Background Information == * The Lady's ability to copy a portion of Sigil and spin it off into a [[demiplane]] in the [[Ethereal plane]] in order to imprison an individual is similar to the [[w:c:ravenloft:Dark Powers|Dark Powers]]' ability to copy a portion of the [[Prime Material plane]] and spin it off into a domain of [[w:c:ravenloft:Ravenloft|Ravenloft]] in the Ethereal in order to imprison an individual. Given the first known domain formed in approximately [[272 BFHR]], well after the first known Maze, it's possible the Dark Powers learned this ability from the Lady. * [[File:LadyKnutsonSketchbook.jpg|thumb|right]] The Lady of Pain's face was chosen as the signature image for Planescape, as a shorthand for its logo. This appears to have been an early design decision, as various shapes for the Lady's head were considered specifically for the logo in [[Dana Knutson]]'s [[Planescape Sketchbook]]. It can be found throughout Planescape material. * The Lady of Pain's alignment was described as [[Lawful neutral]] in some sources<ref name="ettdp14">{{b|D&D|Expedition to the Demonweb Pits|pdf=54341|nip=1|page=14}}</ref>, but this has been contested as unbefitting to the ruler of a realm at the center of the neutral [[Outlands]].

The '''Language Primeval''' is an inherently magical language spoken by the [[Ancient Brethren]], the [[Elder]]s, and other semimythical races that walked the planes when most worlds were young or yet unborn.<ref name="dvd2">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|page=2}}</ref>
The three words of ''Creation Once Spoken'' are perhaps the most powerful utterance in the Language.
[[Iuz]] enacted a ritual written in the Language Primeval which would allow one [[power|demi-power]] to steal power from another, creating a full god. However, the ritual was a lie created by [[Vecna]]: Iuz was instead fully absorbed by [[Vecna]], turning the latter into a Greater Power.<ref name="dvd3">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|page=3}}</ref>
When Vecna was ejected from [[Sigil]] a short time later, the [[Lady of Pain]] shored up the wards of the city to prevent another power trying to "cheat" their way into the city in the same way Vecna did, and in so doing, she shored up the sum of all creation, [[superspace]]. It is the first time she spoke out loud in millennia, rather than through her [[dabus]].<ref name="dvd151">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|page=151}}</ref>

==Description== ''Legends & Lore'' is a comprehensive compendium that explores the mythology and folklore of various cultures, repurposing them for use in ''Advanced Dungeons & Dragons''.
''Legends & Lore'' is an expansion and revision of the earlier work ''[[Deities & Demigods 1st edition|Deities & Demigods]]'', which was first published in 1980. This newer edition, curated by [[James M. Ward]] and [[Troy Denning]], includes expanded content and introduces a number of changes to the format and presentation of the mythological figures, making them more accessible and usable for Dungeon Masters. The book is structured to present each pantheon separately, covering a range of cultures including Norse, Greek, Egyptian, and many others, as well as fictional pantheons created specifically for ''Advanced Dungeons & Dragons''.
''Legends & Lore'' presented a refined selection of content compared to its predecessor, with certain segments, notably those detailing Babylonian, Finnish, Sumerian, and non-humanoid deities, being completely removed. The categorization of mythologies was also adjusted, with the Central American mythos being rebranded as the Aztec mythos, although the Nehwon mythos was preserved. In response to the exclusion of non-human deities from this edition, a subsequent publication titled ''[[Monster Mythology]]'' was released, which offered an in-depth exploration of these divine entities, surpassing the detail found in earlier sources and introducing a variety of new deities.

A '''Lim-Lim''' is a small creature, originally found in the Outlands. Approximately the size of a small dog, their appearance seems to be a cross between a frog and an insect. Their mouths are curved, as though they're always smiling. They are very loyal and friendly, and enjoy being petted. They make a "piyo! piyo!" sound.
A merchant in the [[Marketplace Area]] of the [[Hive]] is known to sell them.
== Planescape: Torment ==
When spoken to in the inventory, the [[Nameless One]] can interact with it: playing with it, setting it down to run around freely, or kicking it. If set down, it will act as a companion, and will attack any nearby enemies.
{{NPC|Marissa||female|medusa|||Society of Sensation|}} can optionally turn one to [[stone Lim-Lim|stone]] for {{NPC|Giltspur||male|human||||}}.

This exotic spice could be purchased as far from Limbo as [[Sigil]], the City of Doors.{{Cite game/Planescape: Torment}} ===Gith and Slaad=== {{/Imagemap}} {{Main|Gith and Slaad}} {{quote|''There, we mold the matter of Limbo with our minds. We forge cities with our thoughts. In its chaos we dwell, with only our '''knowing''' to preserve us. We are the [[githzerai]].''|Dak'kon{{Cite game/Planescape: Torment}}}}
The [[slaad]] were likely natives of Limbo and the [[githzerai]] were immigrants (or refugees, if you ask the [[githyanki]]) and the first layer was named for them. This layer was strategically important because of its connections to [[Gladsheim]], [[Concordant Opposition]], [[Pandemonium]], and the [[Astral plane]]. ===Susanowo=== Named after a deity from the country of Japan on [[Earth]],{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|84}} he ruled a spherical bubble half filled with sea water and aquatic life and churned by storms of his making.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|99}} ===Agni=== Named after a deity from the country of India on [[Earth]],{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|76}} he resided in a sphere of pure flame that floated through the layers at his will. ===Indra=== Also from India,{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|75}} Indra's sphere was half filled with enchanted milk and his palace stood on an island-sized tortoise (or possibly a tortoise-shaped island). ===Lost Gods=== It was unknown if any race or deity favored this layer. ==Cosmology== [[File:Githzerai_limbo_fortress-5e.jpg|thumb|300px|''A githzerai fortress city.'']] ===Afterlife=== {{Main|Afterlife}} When souls arrived in the plane of Limbo, they were not allowed to manifest in some form but rather were absorbed into the matter of the plane. Occasionally a collection of spirits would become powerful enough to form what was called a ''chaos elemental'', not to be confused with a being from the [[elemental planes]]. ==History== According to a thrall captured by [[mind flayer]]s of [[Oryndoll]] beneath [[Andalbruin]], Limbo was the plane to which the [[batrachi]] retreated in {{Yearlink|-31500}}. There, they founded a realm called the [[Supreme Throne]]. [[Cyric]], as a result of his insanity, forcefully moved the fortress into his own [[divine realm]], which became a [[fiendish plane]] according to the [[World Tree cosmology]], or a realm in [[Cocytus]] according to the [[Great Wheel cosmology]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|168}}{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|51-52}} ==Notable Locations== {{fq | text = You want a map of Limbo.
Uh huh.
I suppose you want to know the [[Lady of Pain]]'s address too.
I'd give it to you, but I promised her I wouldn't. | source = [[Factol]] [[Karan]] of the [[Xaositects]]{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|64}} | float = | width = }} The realms of the powers that resided in Limbo floated through the various layers at will and so are listed here in no particular order. * The slaad lords [[Ssendam]] and [[Ygorl]] maintained realms most often found in the first layer but away from areas not under their control. Ssendam's citadel is a golden castle, while Ygorl's realm is a chain of carved spheres that whirl about. * The githzerai formed [[hamlet]]s, [[village]]s, and one large city out of the chaos, known as the Floating City or [[Citadel of Gith]] ruled by [[Zaerith Menyar-Ag-Gith]] (the Great Githzerai). * ''[[Fennimar]]'' was the realm of [[Fenmarel Mestarine]] before moving to [[Arvandor]].{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|111}}{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|143}} [[Shevarash]], the Black Archer, also often stayed there.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|129-130}} * [[Targus]], the [[Netherese]] god of war, lived here,{{Cite book/Netheril: Empire of Magic/Encyclopedia Arcana|33}} before moving to [[Pandemonium]] under his new name of Garagos.{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|18}} * [[Tempus]] Foehammer, Lord of Battles once lived in Limbo.{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|15}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|32}} ''Knight's Rest'' was the name of his realm{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|158}} which later became its own plane named [[Warrior's Rest]] in the [[World Tree cosmology]] model.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|164}} * [[Leira]], the Lady of the Mists, once made her home called the [[Courts of Illusion]] here.{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|11}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|23}}{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|93}} * [[Tapann]], the patron deity of [[korred]]s once made his home here.{{Cite dragon/119/The Ecology of the Korred}} * [[Mystryl]], the Mother of All Magic, lived on this plane in her domain called [[Dweomertor]]{{Cite book/Netheril: Empire of Magic/The Winds of Netheril|49}} until her death in {{Yearlink|-339}}.{{Cite book/Netheril: Empire of Magic/The Winds of Netheril|12}} * [[Astilabor]], the Hoardmistress of the [[Draconic pantheon]], was reputed to have a lair hidden somewhere in Limbo that contained more wealth than that found on all the planets of [[Realmspace]].{{Cite book/Draconomicon (1990)|25}}{{Cite book/Cult of the Dragon|120}}The more recent but Core source ''[[Races of the Dragon]]'' places Astilabor in the [[Outlands]] instead. * [[Kereska]], the draconic "Light of Magic", resided in Limbo.{{Cite book/Draconomicon (1990)|25}} * [[Agni]], the chaotic Vedic [[fire]] deity, had a mutable realm named [[Swarga]] here together with his fellow [[Lords of Creation]] [[Indra]] and [[Vayu]].{{Cite
